text.p: Michael Jordan scored 30 points and Christian Laettner missed a three-pointer with two seconds left as the Chicago Bulls halted the Atlanta Hawks' 20-game home winning streak with an 89-88 victory on Friday.
The Hawks got 19 points and 19 rebounds from Dikembe Mutombo.
Dennis Rodman, who played one game after an 11-game suspension for kicking a cameraman, was not in the starting lineup. Toni Kukoc replaced him and finished with 21 points.
Rodman had two points and 12 rebounds, but fouled out for just the third time in six seasons with 36 seconds left.

In Charlotte, Grant Hill scored 25 of his 29 points in the second half to lead the Detroit Pistons to their eighth victory in their last 11 games, a 109-103 triumph over the Charlotte Hornets in a Central Division matchup.
Joe Dumars and Lindsey Hunter had 20 points each for Detroit, which took advantage of 21 Charlotte turnovers, turning them into 30 points.
Vlade Divac scored 23 points and Glen Rice 21 for the Hornets.
At Minnesota, Chris Carr scored a season-high 22 points and Kevin Garnett added 20 and 11 rebounds as the Minnesota Timberwolves defeated the Orlando Magic, 104-100.
After the Magic used a 10-0 run to tie the game, 94-94, with just over three minutes left, Minnesota responded with five straight points to pull away.
Dean Garrett had 16 points and 14 rebounds for the Timberwolves.

In Toronto, Glenn Robinson scored 37 points and Armon Gilliam added 22, including a pair of free throws with 10 seconds left, as the Milwaukee Bucks edged the Toronto Raptors, 106-102, at Maple Leaf Gardens.
The Raptors had a chance to tie in the final seconds, but Damon Stoudamire's three-point attempt from the left wing bounced high off the rim.
Marcus Camby led the Raptors with 21 points.

In Washington, Rod Strickland scored seven of his 19 points during a 16-2 third-quarter run as the Washington Bullets scored their most points of the season in a 125-107 victory over the New Jersey Nets at Baltimore Arena.
Juwan Howard had 25 points and Calbert Cheaney 22 for the Bullets, who snapped a five-game losing streak and gave new coach Bernie Bickerstaff his first victory.
In San Antonio, Latrell Sprewell scored 32 points and the Golden State Warriors limited San Antonio to just 17 fourth-quarter points in running away with a 108-94 victory over the Spurs.
Joe Smith scored 20 points and grabbed 13 rebounds, and Chris Mullin had 18 points for the Warriors, who blew open a close game with 12-2 run early in the final period.
Dominique Wilkins scored 22 points for San Antonio, which has dropped eight of its last nine games.
In Seattle, Gary Payton scored six of his 23 points during a third-quarter run as the Seattle SuperSonics held Hakeem Olajuwon to a season-low six points and routed the Houston Rockets, 105-85.
Detlef Schrempf added 20 points and Shawn Kemp had 17 for Seattle, which improved to 20-7 at home.

Kemp, the target of recent criticism for tardiness and other off-the-court activities, was ejected with 1:26 left in the third quarter following a scuffle with Houston's Kevin Willis. Willis also was ejected.

In Phoenix, Kevin Johnson scored six of his 27 points in a key first-half run as the Phoenix Suns, bolstered by the return of Jason Kidd, beat the Los Angeles Clippers, 110-93, for their fourth win in five games.
Cedric Ceballos added 24 points and 10 rebounds and Mark Bryant had 16 points for Phoenix, which has won four of five games following a six-game slide. Johnson also had eight assists.
Kidd, who missed 21 games with a hairline fracture of the right collarbone, contributed eight points and nine assists in 22 minutes.
In Vancouver, Shareef Abdur-Rahim scored 31 points and Bryant Reeves added 30 as the Vancouver Grizzlies defeated the Boston Celtics, 109-106, in a meeting of the NBA's worst teams.

Reeves had a big game in the middle for Vancouver, making 13-of-18 shots and grabbing 12 rebounds. Lawrence Moten added 19 points, including several key free throws down the stretch, as Vancouver won consecutive games for the first time this season.
"We felt like we were a lot better inside than them, so we wanted to take advantage of that," Abdur-Rahim said. "We showed that when we (Reeves and I) play together, things can happen."
